newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas sees late burst of trade as prices rise.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas sees late burst of trade as prices rise.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures saw a flurry of activity in the last three minutes of the afternoon session on Tuesday, with 145 lots out of the day's total of 295 traded in this period.

A broker suggested that one player was looking to build a position on the first quarter of 1998, and emerged to take out existing offers in the last minutes before the close, deciding that this was likely to be the best price at which to buy Q1.

The last trades in January, February and March were done respectively at 16.60, 16.70 and 14.20 pence a therm, valuing the whole quarter at a little over 15.80 pence a therm. This is about 0.10 pence a therm below the current price on the OTC market.

Every month from June to March, with the exception of October, traded, an improvement in activity from recent days. Nearly all prices were up where changed, with June seeing the biggest rise, by 0.20 pence a therm. The exception was September, which fell by 0.10 pence.

The forward curve has now taken on a more familiar shape from June onwards, with a backwardation from June to July, followed by contango all the way through from then to February 1998, before switching to backwardation again from February to March. But front month April is still at a discount to the summer, although it was not traded on Tuesday.
A broker expressed some disappointment with the speed at which the contract is developing, saying that the level of business done in the last three minutes on Tuesday should be achieved at all times.

"It's got potential to improve," he said, "but it needs a kick-start." He suggested that it needs a greater level of participation from some of the bigger players in the physical market to improve liquidity.
